handoff: AC1 met (unit 1165, e2e 73, integration green, no test/golden/transcript change). AC2 partial: decide steps.ts:88 builds the log path as spec_dir + recordOf (runs/…) outside the resolver and the lint misses it (F1 blocking); F2/F3 minor.

findings.title: Run log path still joins the spec folder with runs/ outside the resolver, and the AC2 lint does not catch it
findings.detail:
`log_path: `${story.spec_dir}/${recordOf(uf)}/logs/${run_id}.log`` — recordOf returns `uf.record ?? unitRecordPath(uf.unit.dir)`, i.e. `runs/<unit>` or `runs/_story/rounds/NN-<wf>`, so this is a spec folder joined with `runs/` (logs are run state per B2). AC2: 'A repo lint ... fails when a package source outside the resolver's module builds a unit's run-state path by joining a spec folder with `runs/`'. The lint's BY_HAND regex only names RUNS_DIR|unitRecordPath|roundRecordPath, so `${story.spec_dir}/${recordOf(uf)}` passes it. Slice Goal: 'the move to the machine dir (gh-195/05) then changes one function' — this caller would need changing too.
Axis: spec
Suggestion: Build the log path through the pure resolver (e.g. a `runStatePath`-style helper taking the story and the resolved record), and add `recordOf` (or any `${…spec_dir}/${…record…}` join) to the lint with a matcher case.

findings.title: Record paths relative to the spec folder are still derived outside the resolver
findings.detail:
`record: relative(join(root, story.spec_dir), path)` in snapshot.ts:118 and the error message `relative(join(wtPath, story.spec_dir), runsDir)` in packages/cli/src/runtime/act/lifecycle.ts:77 both assume the run-state folder sits under the spec folder. Behaviour is unchanged today, but they will break silently when the folder moves (gh-195/05).
Axis: spec
Suggestion: Have the resolver return the record's spec-relative name (or a display path) alongside the folder, or note these sites for slice 05.

findings.title: AC2 lint matches line by line, so a join split over lines escapes it
findings.detail:
`builds` splits sources on newlines and `\bjoin\([^;]*\b(?:NAMES)\b` needs the name on the same line as `join(`; a multi-line `join(\n  wt,\n  RUNS_DIR)` (as prettier-style wrapping produces) passes.
Axis: standards
Suggestion: Match over the whole source with comments stripped, or at least over each statement.
